Now, the other argument that is often made is that the זוהר was written by משה די ליאון, who lived in Spain in the 13th century, and that he made it up and attributed it to רשב״י in order to make money. This claim actually goes back to the time the זוהר was first published, and it is recorded in the ספר יוחסין by רב אברהם זכות, where he brings the famous testimony of the widow of משה די ליאון. The story is told that רבי יצחק דמן עכו, who was a student of the רמב״ן, came to Spain after Akko was destroyed, and he wanted to investigate the authenticity of the זוהר. He met משה די ליאון, who swore to him that he had the ancient manuscript in his home in Avila. But on the way there, משה די ליאון suddenly died. When רבי יצחק דמן עכו went to Avila, a wealthy man tried to obtain the manuscript by offering to marry his son to משה די ליאון's daughter and support the family, and the widow supposedly said that her husband never had a manuscript, that he wrote it all out of his own head, because if he wrote it under his own name nobody would buy it, but if he attributed it to רשב״י people would pay a fortune for it. Now, how do we answer this argument? First of all, as the ספר יוחסין itself notes, the account breaks off, and we know that רבי יצחק דמן עכו himself, in his later writings such as his sefer מאירת עיניים, quotes the זוהר with tremendous reverence as an authentic ancient work, which shows that by the end of his investigation he was convinced of its authenticity. Furthermore, משה די ליאון wrote many sefarim in Hebrew under his own name, books like שושן עדות and שקל הקודש, and when you compare the Hebrew writings of משה די ליאון to the Aramaic of the זוהר, the two are worlds apart. The depth, the genius, the sweeping scope, and the style of the זוהר are completely different from anything משה די ליאון ever wrote. In fact, in his own Hebrew writings, משה די ליאון actually quotes the זוהר as an ancient authority. Why would someone write the greatest masterpiece in Jewish history, hide his authorship, and then quote it in his own lesser works as an outside source? It makes no sense. Moreover, all the greatest minds of the Jewish people, the רשב״א, the ריב״ש, the בית יוסף, the האר״י הקדוש, the הגר״א, the בעל שם טוב, and the חתם סופר, all recognized the holiness and authenticity of the זוהר. As the חתם סופר famously said, if someone were to tell him that רשב״י did not write the זוהר, then whoever did write it was even greater than רשב״י. As the רד״ל, Rav David Luria, explains in his sefer קדמות ספר הזוהר, while there may have been later additions and marginal notes by copyists that were incorporated over the centuries, the core of the זוהר is an authentic, ancient tradition of תורת הנסתר that goes back to רשב״י.
